lines.text: Level: B1 · Topic: The Construction Site
lines.name: Level: B1 · Topic: The Construction Site

lines.text:
Building a New School

A new primary school is being built on our street. The construction site has been busy for several months, and I often watch the workers from my bedroom window.

Before building started, the construction company put up a tall fence around the site with warning signs that said 'Danger — Construction Site — Keep Out' and 'Hard Hats Must Be Worn'. Inside the fence, bulldozers cleared the land and excavators dug deep trenches for the foundations.

The foundations are the most important part of any building. Workers poured concrete into the trenches and let it set for several days. Once the foundations were solid, they started building the walls using bricks and cement.

A large crane stands in the middle of the site. It lifts heavy steel beams and pallets of bricks to the upper floors. The crane operator sits in a small cabin at the very top — it must be an amazing view!

The workers wear personal protective equipment: hard hats, high-visibility jackets, steel-toed boots, and sometimes ear protection because of the loud machinery. Safety is very important on a construction site.

I noticed that different workers do different jobs. Bricklayers build the walls, electricians install the wiring, plumbers fit the pipes and water systems, and carpenters work with wood for the doors and window frames.

The project manager told my father that the school should be finished by next September. I cannot wait to see the completed building. It is fascinating to watch something being built from nothing.

lines.text: Scene: A site manager shows a new worker around the construction site

lines.text: Welcome to the construction site. Safety first — put on your helmet. Let me show you the heavy machinery.
lines.name: Welcome to the construction site. Safety first — put on your helmet. Let me show you the heavy machinery.

lines.text: Is that a crane lifting the steel beam? It's enormous!

lines.text: Yes — the crane handles the heavy loads. The bulldozer clears the ground, and the excavator digs the foundation.
lines.name: Yes — the crane handles the heavy loads. The bulldozer clears the ground, and the excavator digs the foundation.

lines.text: What about the dump truck and the cement mixer? I see them near the entrance.

lines.text: The dump truck hauls dirt and gravel. The cement mixer pours the cement for the foundation. The forklift moves the brick pallets.

lines.text: UK construction sites are regulated by the Health and Safety Executive (HSE). Strict rules cover protective equipment, working at height, and machinery operation. 'Risk assessment' is a key term — every task must have one.

lines.text: In the UK, skilled trades (plumber, electrician, carpenter, bricklayer) are highly respected. Young people can train through apprenticeships — paid on-the-job training combined with college study. These roles are often well-paid.

lines.text: In the UK, you usually need 'planning permission' from the local council before building or making major changes to a property. 'Listed buildings' (historically important) have even stricter rules.

lines.text: 'Builder's tea' is a strong cup of tea with milk and sugar — the stereotypical drink of British construction workers. It's become a cultural term for any strong, no-fuss cup of tea.

lines.text: Buildings and cranes are 'tall' (not 'high'). The fear is 'heights' (noun) — 'afraid of heights'. 'High' is the adjective for position: 'The bird flew high.'
